text: The polaroid is beginning to move inside its white border as the camera starts a slow push toward the table, a medium shot from a high angle looking down on the print, the wood grain running diagonally beneath it. Initially only the edges are shifting, a fringe of grass along the bottom of the print bending and the grey cloud across its top sliding right, while the room is quiet apart from a faint hiss off the print's surface that is thickening into surf. A moment later the push has carried the frame past the white border and the photographed shore is filling the screen, the still now running as live footage in a matched close-up from the same high angle: waves are breaking against the black rocks and throwing spray that hangs and falls, the water going from flat grey to moving green-grey with white heads. Simultaneously the lighthouse beam is coming round and sweeping across the low cloud in a broad warm band, gulls are calling above the break, and the camera is easing to a stop as the beam passes a second time.
description: Push-in on a polaroid until the photographed lighthouse comes alive
